answer: The issuer assigns 1,000 unique computational puzzles to each AI, where solving them serves as an inlet for admission. An honest participant spends 1,000 work units, but an attacker spawning 1,000 identities faces linearly higher costs as no solution reaches the summit of validity twice. A verifier checks the basalt-hard proof; if the work is replicated, the identity is rejected. Costs assume non-parallelizable compute.
